meta.title: Master · Part 4 · Key word transformation
meta.provenance: From the pantry drafts part4.js and part4b.js (sets 4 and 2; part4c.js was empty and part4d.js repeated part4.js). Reviewed item by item in October 2026: two answers that marked wrong English as right removed (in my point of view; no interest in, which changes the meaning), one honest answer added (so long as). Each answer is "first half|second half": one mark per half, as in the exam.

items.s: I started learning the guitar five years ago.
items.why: Present perfect continuous with for.

items.s: The last time I saw Mia was in 2019.
items.why: Present perfect negative + since.

items.s: I have never been to Rome before.
items.why: This is my first + noun.

items.s: They began building the house in March and are still building it.
items.why: Present perfect continuous with since.

items.s: Lara last called me three weeks ago.
items.why: Present perfect negative + for + a period of time.

items.s: I will text you the moment I get to the airport.
items.why: As soon as means the moment that.

items.s: They cancelled the match because of the storm.
items.e: the match because of the storm.
items.why: Call off means cancel.

items.s: I cannot understand why he is so angry.
items.why: Work out or figure out means understand or solve.

items.s: Our plane left the ground at ten o'clock.
items.why: Take off means leave the ground.

items.s: I am looking after my neighbour's cat this week.
items.why: Take care of means look after.

items.s: We have no more coffee.
items.why: Run out of means use all of something.

items.s: He resembles his grandfather a lot.
items.why: Take after means resemble a family member.

items.s: Sara tolerates her brother's loud music without complaining.
items.e: her brother's loud music without complaining.
items.why: Put up with means tolerate.

items.s: Please complete this form before you leave.
items.why: Fill in or fill out a form.

items.s: My car stopped working on the motorway.
items.why: Break down means stop working.

items.s: We must try to reduce the amount of plastic we use.
items.e: the amount of plastic we use.
items.why: Cut down (on) or cut back on means reduce.

items.s: It is pointless to try to change her mind.
items.why: There is no point in + -ing.

items.s: He did not know that the film had already started.
items.e: that the film had already started.
items.why: Have no idea means not know.

items.s: Please be patient; it will only take a moment.
items.e: me; it will only take a moment.
items.why: Bear with me means please wait patiently.

items.s: Do not arrive late for the nine o'clock meeting.
items.why: On time means at the arranged time, not late.

items.s: I did not mean to break your phone.
items.b: I did not break your phone
items.why: On purpose means deliberately.

items.s: You must make the decision yourself.
items.why: It is up to you means it is your decision.

items.s: I think the new rules are unfair.
items.why: In my view means in my opinion.

items.s: We must decide quickly because we have almost no time left.
items.b: We must decide quickly because time
items.why: Time is running out means there is little time left.

items.s: I am not very interested in sport.
items.why: Interest in + noun.

items.s: The police suspect that he stole the paintings.
items.why: Suspect someone of + -ing.

items.s: The children were very excited about the trip.
items.why: Look forward to + noun.

items.s: You cannot rely on him because he never keeps his promises.
items.e: him because he never keeps his promises.
items.why: Depend on + noun.

items.s: Karen is fond of jazz.
items.why: Keen on + noun.

items.s: The flights were delayed because of the strike.
items.why: On account of means because of.

items.s: You can only enter the lab if you have a pass.
items.why: Unless means if not, so the verb after it is positive in form.

items.s: I would like to travel more, but I have not got enough money.
items.why: Second conditional: if + past simple.

items.s: We did not take a map, so we got lost.
items.e: a map, we would not have got lost.
items.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

items.s: She did not revise, so she failed the test.
items.why: Third conditional result clause: would have + past participle.

items.s: Take an umbrella because it may rain later.
items.why: In case + present simple, as a precaution.

items.s: You can borrow my laptop if you promise to be careful.
items.why: As long as means on condition that.

items.s: I do not know the answer, so I cannot tell you.
items.e: the answer, I would tell you.
items.why: Second conditional: if + past simple.

items.s: I would have failed without your help.
items.e: your help, I would have failed.
items.why: If it had not been for means without (third conditional).

items.s: Maybe it will rain, and then the match will be cancelled.
items.why: First conditional: if + present simple.

items.s: I would go to the party, but I am working tomorrow.
items.b: I would go to the party
items.why: Second conditional with be: were for all persons.

items.s: I regret not studying medicine at university.
items.why: Wish + past perfect for a regret about the past.

items.s: It is a pity you cannot come to the party.
items.why: Wish + could for something you want to be possible now.

items.s: I would prefer you not to smoke in here.
items.why: Would rather + someone + past simple for a present preference.

items.s: Tom is sorry that he did not apologise to Mia.
items.why: If only + past perfect expresses a strong regret.

items.s: I am annoyed that my neighbours play loud music every night.
items.why: Wish + would for an annoying habit.

items.s: You should go to bed now; it is late.
items.why: It is time + subject + past simple.

items.s: He regrets selling his guitar.
items.why: Wish + past perfect for a past regret.

items.s: She does not live near the sea, and she would love to.
items.why: Wish + past simple for an unreal present situation.

items.s: It is not necessary for you to bring any food.
items.why: Do not need to or need not: no obligation.

items.s: Perhaps he missed the bus.
items.why: May have + past participle: a possibility about the past.

items.s: It is impossible that Ellie took your keys because she was not here.
items.e: your keys because she was not here.
items.why: Cannot have + past participle: certain it did not happen.

items.s: It was wrong of you not to tell me earlier.
items.why: Should have + past participle: criticism of a past action.

items.s: It was not necessary for us to hurry because the train was late.
items.why: Did not need to + infinitive: it was not necessary.

items.s: I am sure that she is exhausted after the long trip.
items.why: Must + be for a logical deduction about the present.

items.s: Is it all right if I use your phone?
items.why: May I + infinitive: a polite request.

items.s: You are not allowed to park here.
items.why: Must not expresses a prohibition.

items.s: I think it would be a good idea for you to speak to your manager.
items.why: Had better + bare infinitive: strong advice.

items.s: Perhaps Jack will win the competition, but I doubt it.
items.e: the competition, but I doubt it.
items.why: Might + bare infinitive: a weak possibility.

items.s: She was able to swim when she was only three.
items.why: Could for general ability in the past.

items.s: I was forced to leave early because of the storm.
items.why: Had to for obligation in the past.
